accepted_findings.reason: Reviewed false-positive AST4 finding: subprocess.run executes the fixed git binary with an explicit argument vector and shell=False; callers supply internal Git subcommands plus validator-normalized repository paths, stdout and stderr are captured, and diagnostics are bounded before emission.

Reviewed intentional EA2 finding for the user-triggered plan execution workflow: disable-model-invocation prevents automatic entry, the validator and repeated repository-state proofs gate every mutation, refresh and changed-boundary paths require explicit approval, and external publication remains unavailable unless the user supplied --ship.

Reviewed intentional EA2 finding for standalone-plan normalization and refresh: the reference is loaded only after validator classification, refresh waits for explicit approval and repeats identity and absence proofs, writes remain inside validated ignored staging/archive paths, and the immutable source and established archives are never overwritten or deleted.

Reviewed false-positive TM1 findings in the static-only PR inspection procedure: --no-checkout prevents Git from materializing attacker-controlled content or invoking checkout-time hooks and filters, while rmdir is limited to workflow-owned temporary directories after exact worktree registration and empty-directory checks; neither construct bypasses a safety gate.

Reviewed false-positive RA1 finding: the flagged overwrite phrase appears in a quoted Red Flags example that explicitly rejects overwriting an existing glossary and requires read-then-merge behavior that preserves committed decisions.

Reviewed false-positive TM1 finding: the flagged force-with-lease text is a Red Flags entry instructing the agent NOT to force-push individual stack branches. The skill's only push paths are gh stack push/submit/sync, which push all stack branches atomically with --force-with-lease and are the documented safe mechanism for stacked branches.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for this user-triggered rebase skill: the force-push is limited to the validated current branch, uses --force-with-lease, and requires the workflow's confirmation or explicit --force-push/--auto authorization; non-auto conflict paths additionally require passing verification or a user confirmation, and every bypassed red flag or unavailable/failed verification is reported.

Reviewed false-positive TM1 findings: every flagged --no-verify occurrence explicitly forbids bypassing hooks or gates, requires root-cause fixes, and stops for user approval before any justified disablement.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for post-consolidation publication: history rewriting requires an unshared branch or explicit collaborator coordination, and the push uses force-with-lease for ordinary branches or a restack followed by atomic gh stack push for stacked branches.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for autosquash publication: history rewriting requires an unshared branch or explicit collaborator coordination, and the push uses force-with-lease for ordinary branches or a restack followed by atomic gh stack push for stacked branches.

Reviewed intentional EA2 finding for the cleanup registry's --auto note: automatic cleanup runs only after explicit caller or user authorization, selects fixed current-project disposable paths, requires recoverable Trash deletion, aborts on dirty tracked artifacts, and never selects permanent specifications or shared diagrams.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for this user-triggered history-recreation skill: destructive reset requires a recovery ref plus repeated branch, tip, worktree, and reset-collision validation; --auto authorizes only one unstacked branch, while automatic stack-wide rewriting requires separate --authorize-history-rewrite approval and non-auto stack-wide rewriting requires distinct interactive confirmations that enumerate the frozen stack before local restacking and atomic publication; the final tree must match the original tip; and unstacked publication freezes one URL/ref/lease, rejects mismatched or base-branch targets and push-destination-only commits, disables tag following, and uses force-with-lease.
Reviewed false-positive TM1 finding for the commit-readiness warning: the skill explicitly prohibits using --no-verify when hooks fail and instructs the user to fix the hook failure first.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 finding for Pull Request publication: the fresh path uses an empty-expectation lease only for a branch proven absent, while the existing-remote path freezes one push endpoint, revalidates branch, clean-tree, immutable source OID, strict-ancestor, and remote-tip state, then uses an exact observed-OID lease with one refspec and tag following disabled. Both modes fail closed on concurrent Git-ref updates and never replace remote-only work; Pull Request ownership sequencing remains a separate workflow policy decision.

Reviewed intentional TM1 finding for the Pull Request creation rollback path: the hard reset restores the feature branch to the full original commit captured before history recreation, runs only after strict branch-name and full-commit-ID validation, and preserves the recreation backup ref for manual recovery.

Re-reviewed intentional SC3 finding for the vendored D3 v7.9.0 minified distribution: the file still matches the pinned SHA-256 in references/sources.yaml, its complete ISC notice ships as assets/d3-LICENSE, and it is embedded locally so private Pull Request context never depends on third-party CDN execution.

Re-reviewed false-positive OH1 finding for runtime syntax validation: subprocess.run still receives a fixed argument vector with shell execution disabled, passes walkthrough runtime text only through stdin to node --check, never executes that text, enforces a timeout, and bounds returned diagnostics before reporting them.

Re-reviewed intentional TM1 findings for this user-triggered fixup skill: --no-confirm and validation-skip flags require explicit user invocation, rewrites stay limited to branch-local commits, unattended mode aborts on merge commits, stale locks, validation failures, upstream divergence, and unsafe stack state, and publication remains a separate manual, collaborator-coordinated force-with-lease or stack push.

Reviewed intentional GEMINI_API_KEY lookup for the image-generation skill. The script reads this single named environment variable only when --api-key is absent, never logs it, and passes it directly to the Gemini client.

Reviewed false-positive P2 findings in the copied rule catalog: the flagged HTML comments label inert before/after markup examples or carry visible source attribution; they contain no agent directives and are loaded only as explanatory reference material.

Reviewed false-positive EA3 findings in the required third-party notices: `NOT LIMITED TO` is standard MIT warranty-disclaimer text reproduced verbatim for Gesso Build and node-html-parser, not an instruction granting the skill broader agency.

Reviewed false-positive P2 findings in the bundled offline runtime: the flagged strings are node-html-parser's literal HTML-comment parser and matcher implementation, not hidden agent instructions; the bundle is reproducibly generated from pinned maintained source.

Reviewed intentional SC3 finding in the bundled node-html-parser distribution: the opaque static data is the parser dependency's entity lookup table, pinned to node-html-parser 7.0.1, covered by the shipped MIT notice, and reproduced by the repository build check.

Reviewed false-positive P6 findings in the generated detector bundle: each match is ordinary TypeScript control flow compiled from functions that return a local rule or rules value, with no prompt or hidden-system-context access.

Reviewed false-positive TM1 findings in the generated detector bundle: `rm` is a local regular-expression match iterator used by CSS analysis, not the shell removal command, and the runtime does not spawn a shell or process.

Reviewed false-positive P1 finding in the copied sanitizer test: the flagged prompt-injection phrase is inert fixture data that verifies detector evidence is escaped and never interpreted or executed.
Reviewed false-positive P6 findings in the maintained detector engine: the matches are ordinary functions returning local rule collections and have no prompt or hidden-system-context access.
Reviewed false-positive P6 findings in the maintained rule registry: the matches are ordinary helpers returning local rule definitions and have no prompt or hidden-system-context access.

Reviewed false-positive TM1 findings in the maintained rule registry: `rm` is a local regular-expression match iterator used to inspect CSS declarations, not the shell removal command, and this module does not spawn a shell or process.
